_comment: Row and class counts for the committed dataset (mouse SILAC, n=2 technical replicates per condition). These are DATASET-SPECIFIC EXPECTATIONS, lifted out of bare `assert len(df) == 1948`-style checks that were hardcoded across 8 pipeline source files. Source code should assert against this file, not against inline literals, so that the expected values live in exactly one place. Every number here was verified against the actual committed files under proteomics_de/results/ and General Sheet.xlsx at baseline_git_head. If the input data ever changes, these WILL change -- that is expected, and the correct response is to re-derive and update this file in the same commit as the data change, not to loosen the assertions.
_d7_note: n_up/n_down swapped from 206/509 to 509/206 by the DECISIONS_LOG D7 correction (2026-08-01): the control/treated assignment shipped inverted relative to the lab's own Pilot Project labelling. Verified a pure sign inversion -- limma logFC max|new+old| = 0.0, p-values invariant to 1e-15, NO CHANGE (1223), ON_OFF (10) and the 715-row IPA total all unchanged.
_d11_note: single_condition_rows 606 -> 604 and background_union 2554 -> 2552 by the DECISIONS_LOG D11 correction (2026-08-01): two rows of the raw Light sheet carried a ';'-joined list of bare MaxQuant row indices (32,759 and 681 characters) where an accession belongs. qc/schema.py used to carve an exception so they PASSED validation; they are now quarantined to results/qc/quarantine_accessions.csv and dropped from single_condition_proteins.csv. Discrimination is on token shape (all tokens are bare integers), never length -- the two 69-character 'P08752;P20612;...' rows are legitimate protein groups and are retained. NOTHING ELSE MOVES: the quarantined rows are single-condition, so they never had a fold change, never entered limma, and never reached the IPA export. foldchange_all_rows (1948), qc_limma_rows (1938), ipa_input_rows (715), n_up (509), n_down (206) and onoff_rows (10) are all unchanged; only the enrichment background shrinks, and enrich/enrich_common.py reads background_union from THIS file rather than hardcoding it. The ORA/GSEA artifacts under results/enrichment/ still record 2554 and must be re-queried against the 2552-row background.
_d17_note: New keys added by DECISIONS_LOG D17 (2026-08-03) for the two supplementary exports (export/supplementary_lists.py) that close the gap regulated_up.csv/regulated_down.csv structurally cannot -- a professor review found EGF, EREG missing from DOWN and FRZB missing from UP. tier3_missing_rows (360) = qc_limma.csv rows with n_imputed > 0 (1-2 of 4 raw replicates were zero/missing, so the raw pre-imputation classifier never ran, but limma tested them anyway after MinProb imputation). n_up_partial/n_down_partial (152/96, sum 248) = those 360 reclassified from limma_log2FC at the existing LOG2_THRESHOLD -- FRZB P97401 (+4.407), GAS6 Q61592 (+3.692), LUM P51885 (+2.687) and SLIT3 Q9WVB4 (+2.585) are all in the 152 UP rows, the exact gap reported. 0/360 pass FDR<0.05, consistent with n_significant_fdr05. single_condition_up/down (365/239) sum to single_condition_rows (604); onoff_up/down (7/3) sum to onoff_rows (10). n_qualitative (614) = single_condition_rows + onoff_rows, split n_qualitative_up/down (372/242) per the direction rule UP=treated_only|on_with_treatment (gained after testosterone), DOWN=control_only|off_with_treatment (lost). EGF P01132 and EREG Q61521 are both detected_in=control_only, i.e. direction=DOWN -- the other half of the reported gap. All three protein sets (the core 715, the 248 tier-3, and the 614 qualitative) are pairwise disjoint by construction, verified against the committed files.
_d18_note: New keys added by DECISIONS_LOG D18 (2026-08-13) for the extended QIAGEN uploads (export/ipa_extended.py). The IPA files QIAGEN has were built by etl.foldchange_core.build_ipa_frame, which gates on complete==True BEFORE limma runs, so all 862 proteins D17 recovered (248 tier-3 partial + 614 tier-1/2 qualitative, verified overlap 0) are absent from every upload -- and re-running the pipeline reproduces the same 715 rows rather than fixing it. Three new upload files are added, ADDITIVE ONLY on the D17 precedent: ipa_input.csv, ipa_input_full.csv/.txt, ipa_input_significant.csv, regulated_up.csv and regulated_down.csv stay byte-for-byte untouched (the first is already at QIAGEN), and ipa_extended.py re-hashes all six around every build to prove it. n_ipa_extended (963) = ipa_input_rows (715, values lifted verbatim from ipa_input_full.csv, tier=core) + n_up_partial + n_down_partial (152+96=248, limma's post-imputation estimate, tier=partial) -- the mandatory tier column is what stops an imputed call being read as a complete-case measurement, since the two log2FC columns are different quantities. n_ipa_qualitative_up (372) and n_ipa_qualitative_down (242) equal n_qualitative_up/n_qualitative_down and ship as bare accession lists with NO fold change and NO p-value -- neither is statistically valid when one whole condition has zero data points -- for a separate ID-only IPA Core Analysis, which QIAGEN explicitly supports (research1.md SECTION 3). The three files are pairwise disjoint and their union is 963+372+242 = 1577 distinct accessions; ipa_extended.assert_partition derives that 1577 from these three keys rather than hardcoding it.
_d19_note: n_ipa_background_measured (2552) is the row count of results/ipa_background_measured.txt, the IPA *Reference Set* (export/ipa_extended.py). Uploading it lets a Core Analysis be re-run against the proteome this experiment actually measured instead of QIAGEN's full knowledge base -- without it, the 963/372/242 foreground lists are tested against every gene IPA knows, which overstates enrichment for anything the mass-spec assay was never able to detect. DERIVATION: the union of foldchange_all.csv (1948 rows, quantified in BOTH conditions) and single_condition_proteins.csv (604 rows, quantified in exactly one). The two files are disjoint by accession, so 1948 + 604 = 2552 rows AND 2552 distinct accessions -- which is exactly background_union, deliberately: this is the SAME background enrich/enrich_common.py already passes to g:Profiler as a custom domain_scope (D6/D11), so IPA and the in-house ORA cannot end up testing against two different universes. THE KEY DIFFERS FROM ORA'S: g:Profiler takes one gene symbol per query, so enrich_common projects each row onto its first listed symbol and dedupes to 2530 unique symbols; 22 of the 2552 accessions share a first symbol with another accession, which is the entire 2552 - 2530 = 22 gap. IPA is keyed on UniProt/Swiss-Prot Accession to match the other uploads, so this file keeps the WHOLE accession string including protein groups like 'P05132;P68181' -- taking first tokens would give 2531 single accessions that fail to contain 95 of the 1577 foreground group strings. Hard check: the 2552 are a STRICT superset of the accessions of ipa_input_extended.csv (963), ipa_qualitative_up.txt (372) and ipa_qualitative_down.txt (242); 2552 - 1577 = 975 measured proteins are background-only, and it is those 975 that give the reference set any discriminating power. ADDITIVE ONLY, on the D17/D18 precedent: nothing under results/ is rewritten, and foldchange_all.csv and single_condition_proteins.csv join ipa_extended.BYTE_FROZEN_INPUTS so the build re-hashes them and proves it.
